audit_findings.title: Temporarily low capital spending may be embedded in perpetuity
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 gross property-and-equipment purchases were $415.034 million; 10%-15% of filed 2025 revenue equals $549.639 million-$824.458 million, a computed gap of $134.605 million-$409.424 million, or 13.9%-42.2% of the $970.1 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Capital expenditures are subtracted in owner earnings; carrying temporarily low spending through the explicit forecast and terminal period overstates recurring OE and every scenario's operating PV.
audit_findings.evidence: We historically spend 10% to 15% of our revenue on capital expenditures each year, and we generally expect to continue to maintain a level of capital expenditures that we believe supports our long-term plan for market share growth.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that 2025 spending was below the company's historical range and that 2026 spending is also expected to remain below it while spare network capacity is used. It does not establish that the full historical range is maintenance capital, so the error amount is unresolved. Nevertheless, even the gap to the bottom of the range is large relative to anchor OE and is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Separate maintenance, replacement, capacity, and growth capital spending; forecast each through years 1-10; calculate terminal reinvestment consistent with 2.5% growth and RONTA; then rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Under-reserved self-insurance claims would be an unmodeled senior claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Adverse reserve development would reduce future OE through additional insurance or employee-benefit expense; a credible existing shortfall would also represent a claim ahead of common equity in the valuation bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: These analyses are complex and require significant judgment as the models utilize multiple valuation methods and reflect subjective assumptions, including 1) the weighting of such methods, 2) the loss ratio, 3) the loss trend factor, and 4) the loss development factor, among other assumptions.
audit_findings.explanation: No supplied evidence demonstrates under-reservation. The audited 2025 filing reports $168.8 million of total claims and insurance liabilities, including $138.8 million for BIPD and workers' compensation, and describes independent actuarial testing. The June 2026 filing discloses $80.640 million of current claims accruals but does not separately identify the non-current claims component or an actuarial range, so neither the existence nor materiality of a shortfall can be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 2026 current and non-current claims reserves, obtain paid-and-incurred development triangles and the actuary's reasonable range, compare recorded reserves with that range, and rerun OE and the bridge only for a supported deficiency.

audit_findings.title: Company-owned life-insurance returns may contaminate operating owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 10% market-value sensitivity of $7.9 million pre-tax, computed $5.9 million after tax at the 24.8% effective rate; $98.5 million cash-surrender value less $119.6 million deferred-compensation obligation equals a $21.1 million net liability, about $0.10 per diluted share and 0.15% of $13.914 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unpurged COLI gains or losses affect the OE numerator, while omission of the cash-surrender asset and related deferred-compensation obligation affects the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: A 10% change in market value would have caused a $7.9 million and a $6.8 million impact on our pre-tax income in 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The direction is mixed because COLI gains would overstate OE, losses would understate it, omission of the asset understates the bridge, and omission of the related obligation overstates it. The filed sensitivity is only about 0.6% of anchor OE after tax; even the gross $98.5 million asset is about $0.47 per share and 0.7% of base equity value, while the paired net bridge exposure is about $0.10 per share. On the supplied scale, this is not reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the actual 2025 COLI return into the income statement and confirm its pairing with deferred-compensation expense; document the net bridge treatment, and rerun only if the traced recurring after-tax amount materially exceeds the filed sensitivity scale.
